findings.title: Caller-appended SQL clauses can bypass authorization due to unparenthesized OR expressions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions`, `getFilterConditions`, and `getBaseConditions` (when `filterConditions` is `null`) return `Prisma.Sql` fragments that have top-level `OR` operators without outer parentheses—for example, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` returns `(("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`, and `buildFilterConditions` with only `eventTypeId` returns `("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1)`. Because SQL `AND` has higher precedence than `OR`, any caller that interpolates `getBaseConditions()` into a query alongside additional `WHERE` predicates (e.g., `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${startDate}`) will only apply the trailing `AND` predicate to the right-hand branch of the `OR`, causing the left-hand branch to ignore the additional filter or authorization constraint. Wrap compound `OR` expressions (or the return value of `getBaseConditions` / `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions`) in outer parentheses.

findings.title: Removed caching tests for authorization and filter conditions
findings.body: The `describe("Caching", ...)` block testing that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached `Prisma.Sql` instances on repeated calls was deleted rather than updated to the new `Prisma.sql` format, leaving the caching behavior in `InsightsBookingService` (`cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`) untested.
